question: What regional source evidence does the 2026 mangrove eDNA study provide for Catanduanes, and what must be obtained before any local species rows can be considered?

sourcesReviewed.citation: Nob, C. J. R., et al. (2026). Mangrove-Associated Fish Biodiversity in Selected Philippine Bioregions During the Northeast (Amihan) Monsoon: Insights from eDNA Metabarcoding for Biomonitoring. Environmental DNA, 8(2), e70273. https://doi.org/10.1002/edn3.70273.
sourcesReviewed.sourceType: primary environmental-DNA metabarcoding study across four Philippine mangrove sites
sourcesReviewed.access: Full publisher-hosted article text reviewed. The article says supporting Tables S1 and S2 contain sample collection/environment data and annotated fish OTUs with unique sequence variants and read counts by site. Direct publisher download for the 216.9 KB workbook returned HTTP 403; the table contents were not inspected.

catanduanesSite.siteAsReported: Agojo Point Fish Sanctuary and Marine Reserve, municipality of San Andres, Catanduanes
catanduanesSite.stationDesignAsReported: Three landward, middleward and seaward stations approximately 500 m apart. The paper reports flood (n=3) and ebb (n=3) samples per site; the exact sample-to-station crosswalk must be checked in Table S1.
catanduanesSite.methodsAsReported: Water eDNA metabarcoding using MiFish 12S primers. The article describes negative controls, 99% clustering into OTUs, a minimum of five reads for taxonomic annotation, and species assignment requiring at least 98.5% sequence identity plus monophyletic phylogenetic placement and geographic/context review.
catanduanesSite.reportedSiteMetric: Catanduanes had 11-44 OTUs per sample/site comparison (median 34) in the article's site-level richness summary. These are not 11-44 species and must not be presented as a Catanduanes species count.
catanduanesSite.localSpeciesCrosswalk: Not verified without Table S2, which is described as containing taxonomic OTU assignments and read counts across sampling sites. The article-wide total of 159 species-level OTUs covers all four sites and cannot be assigned to Catanduanes.

sites: Olo-Olo Mangrove Forest and Ecopark, Lobo, Batangas
Agojo Point Fish Sanctuary and Marine Reserve, San Andres, Catanduanes
Katunggan It Ibajay Mangrove Ecopark, Aklan
Iwahig River, Puerto Princesa City, Palawan
nationalStudyContext.studyWideResults: The article reports 276 fish OTUs across four sites, with 159 annotated to species level, 69 to genus, 10 to family, 10 shared between pairs of species and 28 left as unknown. These are study-wide totals, not Catanduanes totals.
taxonomicCautions: Ten study-wide OTUs had identical sequences shared between two species; the authors retained paired provisional annotations.

The authors report seven taxonomically ambiguous species-level OTUs, eight taxa without Philippine distributions documented in FishBase or the Catalogue of Fishes, and ten FishBase-native taxa without matching Philippine literature/Catalogue support.
The article notes eDNA can detect transient or transported DNA; it is not an individual capture, voucher, abundance estimate, resident-population proof or catchability observation.

coverageLimits: This is a single Amihan-season mangrove site in San Andres, not a complete Catanduanes inventory or province-wide reef, river, estuary, lake and coastal survey.
Site-level sample coordinates, exact water measurements and taxon-to-sample/read crosswalks must be taken from the supplementary workbook; do not infer them from the site name or map figure.
A sample-level eDNA detection does not establish a current population, harvest legality, safety, diet, predation or fishing grounds.
The study-wide regional comparison includes Batangas, Aklan and Palawan; do not count those results as Catanduanes evidence.

reuse.articleLicenseEvidence: The existing Crossref metadata review records CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 for the version of record.
reuse.supplementLicense: No distinct license for the supporting workbook was verified in the accessible article metadata.
reuse.disposition: Citation and brief attributed methodology/results only. No table, OTU sequence, raw read count, species list or derived app row copied. No Bangwit publication approval.

disposition.reason: The article establishes a dated Catanduanes fringe-mangrove sampling lead, but the sample-to-OTU crosswalk needed for local taxa is in an inaccessible supporting workbook and the reuse terms do not grant derivative/publication permission.

nextAction: Obtain the authors' Table S1/S2 workbook through an accessible official route; verify Catanduanes sample IDs, station/tide/date/environment records, taxonomic annotations, read counts, sequence variants, and any sample coordinates. Review supporting-file rights separately. Keep this source available in both the Bicol and national cross-region coastal queue, and continue Catanduanes reef, river/estuary and inland-water screening in parallel.

sources.supports: Full article metadata and methods: date and site identity, sampling window/design, habitat type, eDNA method, study-wide results, Catanduanes site-level OTU richness and limitations.
Official Table S1-S2 download endpoint; publisher returned HTTP 403, so no sample or taxon rows were inspected.
Existing Crossref metadata record indicates CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 for the article version of record; this does not establish a separate supporting-file license.
